title: Sell Mineral Rights in Birney, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Birney, MT
metaDescription: Birney sits along the Tongue River in Rosebud County near Northern Cheyenne land. A retired E&P engineer explains what real ownership and development history looks like here.
heroLead: Birney is small, remote, and along the Tongue River, and I've found the honest answer for most owners here is that their interest has never seen a permit, let alone a well.
intro: Down along the Tongue River in southern Rosebud County, Birney sits near Northern Cheyenne tribal land in a sparsely populated stretch that has seen limited oil and gas activity historically. I'd rather set that expectation clearly than let an owner think a modest ranch-country tract here carries the same near-term value as land near an active CBM field.

sections.heading: Ranch Country First, Mineral Country a Distant Second
paragraphs: The Tongue River valley around Birney is cattle and hay ground, and most mineral title here traces to homestead-era patents severed at some point over the decades. Coalbed methane development in Rosebud County has concentrated farther north near Colstrip, and Birney has largely sat outside that activity.

sections.heading: Checking for Trust Land Overlap
paragraphs: Given the proximity to Northern Cheyenne Reservation boundaries, I'd confirm whether a specific tract near Birney is fee land or carries any trust history before discussing value, the same way I would anywhere near a reservation edge. It's a quick check that avoids assumptions in either direction.

sections.heading: An Honest Range for a Quiet Area
paragraphs: For most Birney-area interests, I'd expect a modest, speculative value tied to long-term potential rather than current production, since there's little to no drilling history nearby. If your family does have an old lease or any historical royalty payments on record, that changes the picture, and I'd want to see that documentation specifically.

faqs.question: Is there any oil and gas history near Birney, MT?
faqs.answer: Very little. This part of southern Rosebud County has largely sat outside the coalbed methane development that concentrated farther north near Colstrip.

faqs.question: Should I check if my Birney-area interest is trust land?
faqs.answer: Yes, given the proximity to Northern Cheyenne Reservation boundaries. A title search at the Rosebud County Clerk and Recorder in Forsyth will show the recorded fee chain, and any allotment history in your family is worth following up on with the relevant BIA office.

faqs.question: My family has never received a royalty check on land near Birney. Is our interest worthless?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily worthless, but it is a more speculative interest without current income, valued on long-term potential rather than production. I'd give you an honest range reflecting that rather than imply near-term drilling interest that isn't there.
